summary: lib/lane.sh runs one milestone as its own process (exit 0/10-15, reason in state/lanes/<m>/exit); lib/driver.sh is the coordinator (poll, reap, open under MAX_LANES, end reasons, finish waits for lanes, removes slots). Shared code moved to lib/record.sh. Per-lane units, scratch, prompt files; metrics rows carry lane. Opus review: 5 fixes. Suite 423 → 432, green.
verified_how: check.sh: green in 256 s, 432/432 (TEST_JOBS=4). New 37-lanes-run.sh 9/9; 3 of its first 4 checks fail on HEAD's code, the verify-snapshot check failed before its fix. bash -n on lane.sh driver.sh record.sh and the touched tests; node --check metrics.mjs.

dead_ends.tried: setting BRANCH to the lane branch in the lane process
dead_ends.why: gh_url then linked notifications to the lane branch; BRANCH stays the record's, HARNESS_BRANCH names the lane

dead_ends.tried: deleting every lane branch with nothing beyond main at finish
dead_ends.why: a parked lane's pushed branch is what 36's --base check (and a continue) reads; only never-pushed ones go (D11)

discoveries.text: A lane's normal close leaves its services up (plan D4): its EXIT trap tears them down only when it dies without an exit line. finish and the coordinator's pause and long limit waits stop what closed lanes left (lanes_services_down).
The coordinator syncs the record (fetch, push) only when it may open a lane or while paused (D9); lanes sync before each session. P2's multi-lane admission must keep that rate in mind.
The MAX_REPAIRS streak is per lane process now, not run-wide.
Suite: 432 checks, 256 s wall at TEST_JOBS=4 (was 423 in ~231 s); 37-lanes-run.sh adds ~35 s of slot time.
